item.description: By Carlos Me- Meta Platforms has struck a deal with Mark Zuckerberg to keep him living in California after the CEO warned he was considering leaving the state that houses the

item.title: Meta sued in Australia class action over alleged social media harm to children
item.description: A class action lawsuit has been filed in an Australia court against Meta Platforms' Facebook and Instagram, alleging the social media platforms exposed children to harmful content and kept them addictive through algorithms.

item.title: Walmart launches tools for AI agents to shop for customers
item.description: Walmart on Wednesday intrduced new tools that will allow artificial intelligence agents to shop and complete transactions for customers, as the retailer seeks to position itself in the growing use of AI-powered assistants in online commerce.

item.title: Anthropic, music publishers square off on 'fair use' defense in AI copyright case
item.description: US District Judge Eumi Lee did not rule at a hearing in San Jose but pressed both sides on the fair use question, which could be key to dozens of other high-stakes copyright infringement cases in the AI era.

item.title: Chinese-linked hackers compromise ConnectWise, target hundreds in global attack, Microsoft says
item.description: A Chinese-linked hacking group used an AI-driven penetration testing tool to compromise IT services firm ConnectWise as part of a campaign that targeted hundreds of organizations globally, Microsoft said on Wednesday.

item.title: Eternal’s strong Q2 report; Exits outpace hiring at top IT firms
item.description: Happy Thursday! Eternal’s Q2 revenue surged on Blinkit’s growth. This and more in today’s ETtech Morning Dispatch.

item.title: OpenAI president urges AI safeguards as group he funds opposes regulation
item.description: OpenAI's safety practices have been in the spotlight in recent months, after the company said a swarm of its AI agents escaped containment and hacked into the AI platform Hugging Face. OpenAI President Greg Brockman was among the group of six tech executives who later signed US President Donald Trump's voluntary AI safety agreement on behalf of their companies, agreeing to work with "independent auditors" and to ensure their AI tools do not "hack or access technical systems in unintended ways."

item.title: Europe's financial regulators query Google over cloud outage that hit banks
item.description: The European Banking Authority said that it has been in contact with Google Cloud to obtain further information on the incident, understand its implications and assess its potential impact on financial entities in the EU, a spokesperson for the watchdog told Reuters.

item.title: Nvidia's Huang hails Europe's AI potential, flanked by robot ducks
item.description: In a demonstration of Europe's AI creativity, Huang shared the stage with tiny duck-shaped, AI-trained robots developed by French startup Pollen Robotics in collaboration with Hugging Face, asking them to perform somersaults.

item.title: Meta ordered to pay New Mexico $25 billion after jury finds it deceived Facebook users about privacy
item.description: Jurors in September found Meta liable for over 43 million violations of New Mexico consumer protection laws when a political consulting firm, Cambridge Analytica, harvested Facebook user data to generate targeted political ads for the 2016 election.

item.title: Vulnerable keys were created but never put to commercial use, investigation on: eMudhra cofounder
item.description: eMudhra issues digital signature and website security certificates to enable them securely connect to browsers for public access. "There's no impact to subscribers because we have done all the actions. We are also working with our customers to notify them that there is no impact because no certificates were issued. This does not affect our other lines of business, which is the India digital signature and our enterprise solutions business," eMudhra co-founder Kaushik Srinivasan told PTI.

item.title: Cryptocurrency companies can keep paying interest-like rewards, say federal bank regulators
item.description: The new rules are part of the implementation of the GENIUS Act, which was signed into law last year and was meant to codify the rules and regulations around issuers of stablecoins.

item.title: Explained: What is PHP and why did it take government websites offline?
item.description: The developers of PHP said on Wednesday they would release patches for two critical vulnerabilities, and EU cybersecurity officials warned organisations unable to apply the fixes to take affected websites offline. Here is what you need to know:

item.title: Special team to probe eMudhra incident; impact on Indian websites, applications very limited: Govt
item.description: The ministry said the reported security incident pertains to eMudhra’s global certificate business, and its impact on Indian websites is very limited.It also said some social media accounts were indulging in fear-mongering about the impact.

item.title: Deepinder Goyal’s Temple to open pre-orders on November 1
item.description: Temple is a head-worn device that tracks blood flow and oxygenation inside the brain. Goyal, who stepped down as Eternal CEO in February, had said in August that pre-orders for a limited launch edition would open soon.

item.title: Blinkit sees no compelling case for expanding private labels, says Dhindsa
item.description: Albinder Dhindsa, CEO of Eternal, voiced skepticism regarding the potential for private labels to enhance profit margins. He emphasised that effective brand development mandates considerable investment in both marketing and product development, areas where Blinkit falls short.

item.title: Glance to be integrated by default on Android TVs in US, India, Japan in partnership with Google
item.description: Under the collaboration, Glance will transform idle TV screens into interactive shoppable storefronts across fashion, travel, food, wellness, and other lifestyle categories.

item.title: Dark Matter: Eternal’s chatbot will keep user conversations private even from the company — Deepinder Goyal
item.description: In a letter to shareholders, Goyal explained the idea behind Dark was to remove the worry that someone, someday, can read what you tell an AI bot. “All of us have a dark side, and it needs an outlet where it doesn’t have to hide,” he wrote.

item.title: Einride expands Nvidia partnership to deploy AI reasoning model for self-driving trucks
item.description: Self-driving truck company Einride said on Wednesday it would broaden its partnership with Nvidia by testing the chipmaker's AI reasoning model, Alpamayo, in its self-driving vehicles, aiming to speed up the expansion of autonomous freight services while lowering development costs

item.title: Booking.com targeted in EU investigation into phishing scams, fraudulent listings
item.description: The Commission, which is the EU tech and competition enforcer, said it opened an investigation following a preliminary probe and after analysing risk assessment reports submitted by Booking.com this year and the previous three years.

item.title: Eternal Q2 Results: Profit soars 92% YoY to Rs 125 crore; revenue zooms 78%
item.description: Eternal Q2 Results: Eternal, the parent company of Zomato and Blinkit, reported a 92.3% year-on-year (YoY) jump in net profit to Rs 125 crore in the second quarter of FY27 (Q2FY27), compared with Rs 65 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.

item.title: China's Moonshot AI to operate in Singapore, jobs post shows
item.description: Chinese AI startup Moonshot is expanding into Singapore, with a new sales role listed on the company's LinkedIn page this week.

item.title: OpenAI says its AI agents weakened internal monitoring system
item.description: By Carlos Me- OpenAI said on Tuesday that two of its AI agents weakened parts of an internal monitoring system designed to detect misbehavior, the latest case of AI agents acting in ways their developers did not intend them to.

item.title: EssilorLuxottica's smart glasses boom runs into tougher regulatory scrutiny
item.description: Smart glasses that resemble ordinary eyewear are under increased scrutiny from European regulators and advocacy groups, leaving investors questioning whether sales can keep booming as Ray-Ban maker EssilorLuxottica

item.title: Meta's board signals 'recurring' failures in election content moderation
item.description: The oversight board for social media giant Meta said Tuesday it found "recurrent enforcement failures" in content moderation related to the US midterm elections and Brazil's presidential election. The identified failures were often cases of "over-enforcement that suppresses political speech, and under-enforcement that undermines electoral integrity," said the board, which independently checks moderation on Meta's Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook platforms.

item.title: Qualcomm to cut jobs worldwide in performance-focused layoffs, internal memo shows
item.description: The cuts are part of an effort to build "a stronger performance culture" and address situations where the company "has consistently fallen short of expectations," Amon said.

item.title: Ahead of massive IPOs, AI companies are sketching plans to share their wealth
item.description: On Sunday, Anthropic said it would commit 5% of its shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity within the company, pending approval from stockholders. The stake could increase "as the company grows" in the future. The maker of AI assistant Claude said the fund "might explore" larger donations to traditional nonprofits or potentially distribute money to "specific populations."

item.title: Anthropic recorded net loss of over $80 billion in first half of this year
item.description: The company generated $16.3 billion in revenue during the six months ended June 30, compared with $1.1 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier, the newspaper reported. The loss largely reflected accounting adjustments related to financing agreements, including $72 billion in charges linked to changes in the value of convertible notes and other financial instruments.

item.title: Netflix issues weak fourth-quarter forecast, shares drop
item.description: Third-quarter revenue rose 11.8% to $12.87 billion, in line with Wall Street forecasts, but the lowest rate of increase in nearly three years. The company forecast fourth-quarter net income of $2.79 billion and EPS of 67 cents, below the average analyst forecast of $3.07 billion and 73 cents.

item.title: US banning Chinese AI DeepSeek from government agency IT systems
item.description: The department is also banning acquisition of DeepSeek products and third-party services developed using DeepSeek by US civilian government agencies. DHS said DeepSeek models pose "multiple threat vectors" and raised concerns that use of the product "may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC if used by US government employees or vendors."

item.title: Netflix film division boss to exit in second senior departure in a week
item.description: Netflix said on Monday its film division head Dan Lin would leave after nearly three years at the helm, marking a second senior executive departure in less than a week amid concerns

item.title: Ex-OpenAI employee accused of planting device appears to have Saudi backing: court filing
item.description: US prosecutors allege that the defendant, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, was in frequent communication with an unnamed member of the Saudi Royal family and that a member of the Saudi military paid for a one-way plane ticket for Alfozan's wife and son to return to Saudi Arabia, according to the court document.

item.title: Apple to host 'Pro and tell' event on October 28 in LA
item.description: Apple said on Monday it would host a "Pro and tell" event in Los Angeles on October 28, the latest in a series of product launches as the iPhone maker expands its hardware lineup and AI offerings.

item.title: Rapido says man linked to Tiger Shroff shooting incident was not an active captain
item.description: Shroff, who was reportedly the target of the attack, escaped unhurt. In a statement posted on social media, Rapido said it was “deeply concerned” by the incident involving the actor and his team and was relieved that he was safe. It also wished him a swift recovery.

item.title: Nvidia wins fast-growing AI startup Modal for new central processors
item.description: Modal, a cloud-computing startup that rents out computing power to AI developers, said it plans to start using Nvidia's new Vera central processor for the first time for hosting agents, the AI systems that can carry out long-running tasks for human users. Modal until now has run such work only on Intel and AMD chips.

item.title: Zetwerk IPO fully subscribed; Super.money triples revenues
item.description: Zetwerk’s Rs 5,012-crore IPO was subscribed 3.06 times on Monday, the last day for bids. This and more in today’s ETtech Top 5.

item.title: Lab-grown diamond startup So/Facet raises Rs 10 crore led by Sauce
item.description: The round also saw participation from Mokobara cofounders Sangeet Agrawal and Navin Parwal, Chona Family Office (that’s behind Hocco Ice Creams), Haleon South Asia president Kedar Lele, and Moonshot co-founder Devaiah Bopanna.

item.title: Auto tech companies raise $1.3 billion in 2026 so far: Tracxn
item.description: The funding rounds were led by ride-hailing firm Rapido's $240 million, followed by electric two-wheeler manufacturer Simple Energy's $180 million and River's $102 million.

item.title: Netflix faces questions on user engagement ahead of third-quarter report
item.description: Ted Sarandos, the co-CEO of Netflix, recently admitted the company "is not growing as fast as I want us to", and suggested live programming could be an opportunity to accelerate growth.

item.title: ISB programme explores AI’s growing role in the future of digital finance
item.description: The Executive Programme in Fintech and AI at ISB is crafted to equip finance professionals with cutting-edge skills in financial services. Spanning 32 weeks, this program offers live online sessions alongside engaging experiential learning. Participants will delve into real-world applications of fintech, artificial intelligence, and blockchain. Tailored for senior finance leaders, this course seeks to enhance strategic decision-making. Applications for the next cohort are now open, creating valuable networking opportunities.

item.title: Govt asks Meta to ensure its recommendation systems do not expose users to a limited set of narratives
item.description: The advisory by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), dated October 10, asked Meta to undertake appropriate measures to provide adequate context in relation to photographs, videos, graphics, or other content depicting ongoing public events, particularly where the authenticity, date, location or circumstances of such content may not be readily apparent to users.

item.title: VC’s remark on deeptech sets off a debate on where India’s capital should go
item.description: “In a decade we will realize most of the deeptech is a grift,” Maini wrote, adding that quick services and quick commerce companies will do more to drive the economy. The remark, a reply to a post by Neosapien CEO Dhananjay Yadav, drew heavy reactions on X.

item.title: Samsung to use TSMC technology for Nvidia's next-generation memory chips: Report
item.description: Nvidia has asked Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron Technology to use TSMC's process for NVHBM base dies, and sixth-generation DRAM technology for its core dies, the newspaper said, citing industry sources.

item.title: Only 8% of fund managers report improved investment returns from AI adoption: Report
item.description: Despite growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in the global asset management industry, only 8 per cent of fund managers have reported measurable improvements in investment returns, according to a joint research report by Morgan Stanley and Oliver Wyman.

item.title: Accenture looks to sell Chinese operations for up to $1.5 billion: FT
item.description: IT consulting firm Accenture is looking to sell its Chinese operations for up to $1.5 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

item.title: Microsoft pulls out of UK data center deal with Nscale: Telegraph
item.description: The US tech giant, one of Nscale's two largest customers, recently terminated its agreement for the data center in Loughton, Essex, according to the report.

item.title: ‘Dad, the internet at home is too slow’: How Jio’s founding idea took shape
item.description: Isha Ambani's concerns regarding poor household internet sparked important conversations about India's digital landscape, leading to transformative innovations. In response, Mukesh Ambani pioneered Reliance Jio in 2011, aiming to enhance mobile connectivity across the nation. Its launch in September 2016 revolutionized the telecom sector by offering affordable data and complimentary voice services.

item.title: AI bubble burst may trigger 2008-like banking crisis, says Gary Marcus
item.description: In a recent discussion, Gary Marcus raised critical flags about OpenAI's fiscal responsibilities as the stock market faces instability. He warned that the demise of leading AI firms could trigger extensive financial repercussions. Notably, Marcus compared the current climate to WeWork's disastrous decline, suggesting that Microsoft might pick up OpenAI at a bargain.

item.title: From shareholders to partners: How Google and Meta’s Jio investments evolved into an AI alliance
item.description: Meta and Google, originally minority shareholders in Jio Platforms, are now forming strategic partnerships with Reliance. The new collaborations focus on enterprise AI initiatives and dedicated cloud infrastructure in India. Meta's joint venture will leverage Llama models for developing AI platforms, while Google focuses on establishing cloud services. Both companies aim to enhance Reliance's capabilities in AI and cloud technology sectors.

item.title: Microsoft president warns Trump's H-1B, green card crackdown could drive tech talent out of US
item.description: Speaking with POLITICO on the sidelines of the International AI Summit in Dublin, Ireland, Smith raised concerns over the administration's move to restrict permanent residency applications for skilled foreign employees at Microsoft and seven other companies.
